_comment: Agentic toolkit hooks proposal. NOT loaded by the harness. Reference-only until MVP gate is lifted (see docs/agentic-toolkit.md). To activate: copy the 'hooks' object into .claude/settings.json (merge with existing keys), then verify with 'Stop' a session and re-enter.

hooks.command: python3 .claude/skills/obsidian-project-management/lifecycle.py list --status review --milestone MVP 2>/dev/null | head -20 && echo '---' && python3 .claude/skills/obsidian-project-management/lifecycle.py list --status blocked --milestone MVP 2>/dev/null | head -20

PostToolUse._comment_purpose: Surface the validation_command of the in-progress task whenever an Edit hits Android/iOS source. Hint, not a blocker.

hooks.command: bash -c 'PATH=$1; case "$PATH" in android/*|ios/*) python3 .claude/skills/obsidian-project-management/lifecycle.py list --status in-progress 2>/dev/null | head -5 ;; esac' _ "${CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT_PATH:-}"

Stop._comment_purpose: Warn if there are uncommitted changes while an Obsidian task is still in-progress. Soft signal, never blocks Stop.

hooks.command: bash -c 'IN_PROGRESS=$(python3 .claude/skills/obsidian-project-management/lifecycle.py list --status in-progress 2>/dev/null | wc -l); UNCOMMITTED=$(git status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | wc -l); if [ "$IN_PROGRESS" -gt 0 ] && [ "$UNCOMMITTED" -gt 0 ]; then echo "warn: $IN_PROGRESS task(s) in-progress with $UNCOMMITTED uncommitted file(s)"; fi'

_activation_steps: 1. Lift the gate in docs/agentic-toolkit.md (status: gated -> active).
3. Add a top-level 'hooks' key with the contents of the 'hooks' object above (drop the _comment_* keys).
4. Confirm none of the hook commands appear in permissions.deny.
5. Restart the session and verify SessionStart prints the briefing.
6. Run a tiny Edit on android/** or ios/** and confirm PostToolUse fires.
_safety_notes: Hooks run as the current user. Inspect each command before merging.
All three hooks here are read-only and never block tool use.
If 'lifecycle.py list' is slow on a big vault, raise the timeouts.
Hook output goes to the user-visible stream; PII in task titles will appear there.
